**rtfreporter turns the tables you already make in R -- an ARD from
cards / cardx, an rtables / tern or a gtsummary table -- into clinical RTF
files: running header and footer, page numbers, titles and footnotes
included.**

## Why rtfreporter?

- **Your packages' tables, straight to RTF**: cards / cardx ARDs, rtables /
  tern, rlistings, gtsummary, gt, tfrmt, flextable, huxtable, data frames.
- **ARD first**: an ARD becomes a table in a few lines, `(N=xx)` included.
- **Submission-ready pages**: running headers and footers, titles, footnotes,
  pagination, listings and figures.
- **One deliverable**: outputs assembled with a cover page, a clickable table
  of contents and PDF bookmarks
  ([how](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/assembling.html)).
- **Small, on purpose**: one clinical layout, base R only.

## Installation

Not on CRAN yet; from GitHub:

``` r
remotes::install_github("ichirio/rtfreporter@v0.8.2")   # the latest release
remotes::install_github("ichirio/rtfreporter")          # the development version
```

## From an ARD to an RTF table in 30 seconds

The ARD is the input, made with
[cards](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/) /
[cardx](https://insightsengineering.github.io/cardx/) before rtfreporter.
From there it is three steps:

<!-- flow: the same in README.md, vignettes/rtfreporter.Rmd and vignettes/articles/tables-from-ard.Rmd (tests/testthat/test-docs-flow.R) -->
<div class="rtf-flow">
<table>
<tr>
<td><strong>The ARD</strong><br>made with cards / cardx</td>
<td><strong>1. The table</strong><br><code>ard |&gt;</code><br><code>normalize_ard() |&gt;</code><br><code>table_plan() |&gt;</code><br><code>plan_*()</code></td>
<td><strong>2. The report</strong><br><code>rtf_document() |&gt;</code><br><code>rtf_section() |&gt;</code><br><code>rtf_tables(plan)</code></td>
<td><strong>3. The RTF file</strong><br><code>generate_rtfreport()</code></td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<!-- /flow -->

The page they write:

<p align="center">
  <img src="man/figures/readme-ard-example.png"
       alt="The t_dm.rtf written by the code below, opened in a word processor: a running header with Ichirio Pharma | Study XYZ-001, DRAFT and Page 1 of 1, then Table 14.1.1, the title and the population; three arm columns with (N=86), (N=84), (N=84) read from the ARD, age as Mean (SD), Median and Min, Max and sex as n (%); the footer gives the program's path and the run date."
       width="720" />
</p>

The code:

``` r
library(rtfreporter)
library(cards)

# (ARD): made with cards / cardx -- data preparation, outside rtfreporter
adsl <- ADSL
adsl$ARM <- factor(adsl$ARM, c("Placebo", "Xanomeline Low Dose", "Xanomeline High Dose"))
ard <- ard_stack(adsl, .by = ARM,
                 ard_summary(variables = AGE),
                 ard_tabulate(variables = SEX))

# 1. the table, straight from the ARD
plan <- ard |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous  = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})",
                             "Median"    = "{median:.1f}",
                             "Min, Max"  = "{min:.0f}, {max:.0f}"),
             categorical = "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%}%)", notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_labels(c(AGE = "Age (years)", SEX = "Sex, n (%)")) |>
  plan_stub() |>
  plan_col_header(values = list(n = TRUE), rtf_col_header(c("", "{col}\n(N={n})")))

# 2. the report: the document around the table
report <- rtf_document(
  program = "/studies/XYZ-001/programs/tfl/t_dm.R",
  tokens  = list(STUDY = "XYZ-001")) |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(list(
      c(l = "Ichirio Pharma | Study {STUDY}",      r = "DRAFT"),
      c(l = "Protocol: {STUDY} (CDISC pilot data)", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
      c(c = ""),
      c(c = "Table 14.1.1"),
      c(c = "Demographic Characteristics"),
      c(c = "<Safety Analysis Set>"))),
    footer = rtf_footer(list(
      c(l = "N = number of subjects in the analysis set; percentages are based on N."),
      c(l = "SD = standard deviation."),
      c(l = "{PROGRAM_FULL}    Generated on: {DATETIME}")))) |>
  rtf_tables(plan)

# 3. the RTF file
generate_rtfreport(report, "t_dm.rtf")
```


The arms' `(N=xx)` come from the ARD: `ard_stack(.by = )` counts them.  The
same code pages a long table, sorts an adverse-events table by frequency,
and can be saved and reused:
[Get started](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/rtfreporter.html),
[Tables from an ARD](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/tables-from-ard.html),
and more tables, listings and figures in the
[Gallery](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/gallery.html).

## An rtables / tern table

``` r
library(tern)

adsl$SEX <- factor(adsl$SEX)
lyt <- basic_table(show_colcounts = TRUE) |>
  split_cols_by("ARM") |>
  analyze_vars(c("AGE", "SEX"), var_labels = c(AGE = "Age (years)", SEX = "Sex, n (%)"),
               .stats   = c("mean_sd", "median", "range", "count_fraction"),
               .labels  = c(mean_sd = "Mean (SD)", median = "Median", range = "Min, Max"),
               .formats = c(mean_sd = "xx.x (xx.xx)", median = "xx.x", range = "xx, xx",
                            count_fraction = "xx (xx.x%)"))

rtf_document(
  program = "/studies/XYZ-001/programs/tfl/t_dm_tern.R",
  tokens  = list(STUDY = "XYZ-001")) |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(list(
      c(l = "Ichirio Pharma | Study {STUDY}",      r = "DRAFT"),
      c(l = "Protocol: {STUDY} (CDISC pilot data)", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
      c(c = ""),
      c(c = "Table 14.1.1"),
      c(c = "Demographic Characteristics"),
      c(c = "<Safety Analysis Set>"))),
    footer = rtf_footer(list(
      c(l = "N = number of subjects in the analysis set; percentages are based on N."),
      c(l = "SD = standard deviation."),
      c(l = "{PROGRAM_FULL}    Generated on: {DATETIME}")))) |>
  rtf_tables(as_rtftables(build_table(lyt, df = adsl))) |>
  generate_rtfreport("t_dm_tern.rtf")
```

       width="720" />
</p>

## A gtsummary table

``` r
library(gtsummary)

tbl <- tbl_summary(adsl, by = ARM, include = c(AGE, SEX),
                   type      = AGE ~ "continuous2",
                   statistic = list(AGE ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", "{median}", "{min}, {max}"),
                                    SEX ~ "{n} ({p}%)"),
                   digits    = list(AGE ~ c(1, 2, 1, 0, 0), SEX ~ c(0, 1)),
                   label     = list(AGE ~ "Age (years)", SEX ~ "Sex")) |>
  add_stat_label(label = list(AGE ~ c("Mean (SD)", "Median", "Min, Max"), SEX ~ "n (%)")) |>
  modify_header(label ~ "", all_stat_cols() ~ "{level}\n(N={n})") |>
  remove_footnote_header(columns = all_stat_cols())

rtf_document(
  program = "/studies/XYZ-001/programs/tfl/t_dm_gtsummary.R",
  tokens  = list(STUDY = "XYZ-001")) |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(list(
      c(l = "Ichirio Pharma | Study {STUDY}",      r = "DRAFT"),
      c(l = "Protocol: {STUDY} (CDISC pilot data)", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
      c(c = ""),
      c(c = "Table 14.1.1"),
      c(c = "Demographic Characteristics"),
      c(c = "<Safety Analysis Set>"))),
    footer = rtf_footer(list(
      c(l = "N = number of subjects in the analysis set; percentages are based on N."),
      c(l = "SD = standard deviation."),
      c(l = "{PROGRAM_FULL}    Generated on: {DATETIME}")))) |>
  rtf_tables(as_rtftables(tbl)) |>
  generate_rtfreport("t_dm_gtsummary.rtf")
```

The same table again, its labels and headers set in gtsummary
([the page it writes](man/figures/readme-gtsummary-example.png)).  gt,
tfrmt, flextable and huxtable tables, rlistings listings and plain data
frames go in the same way: see
[Importing tables](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/importing-tables.html)
and the *same report, every framework* articles for
[Demographics](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/showcase-dm.html)
and [Adverse events](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/showcase-ae.html).

## Writing rtfreporter code with an AI assistant

rtfreporter is too new to be in any chat model's training data: asked for
rtfreporter code it reaches for `r2rtf`'s verbs or invents arguments, and
flags neither as a guess.  Give it the facts first.

The manuals **ship with the package**, so the one you attach describes the
version you actually have:

``` r
rtfreporter_ai_manual()                     # path to the user manual
rtfreporter_ai_manual("ai-kit", ard = ard)  # a folder to attach: the request, the manual,
                                            # three example programs, your ARD and its shape
```

Or download it -- **[AI user manual (v0.8.2)](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/ai/rtfreporter-ai-user-manual-0.8.2.md)** -- one self-contained file sized for a single chat session.  Attach it at the **start** of the session and say *"use this manual"*.  [`ai/rtfreporter-ai-user-manual.md`](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/ai/rtfreporter-ai-user-manual.md) always resolves to the newest release, so it is safe to bookmark; the development copy is published beside it under its own version.

Every example in it is run by CI and its function list is checked against
`NAMESPACE`, so a manual that drifts from the API fails the build.

Working *on* rtfreporter rather than with it?  See [Developing with an AI assistant](https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/ai-development.html), which covers the companion **developer** manual (`rtfreporter_ai_manual(which = "dev")`).

## A focused tool, on purpose

rtfreporter is a focused tool for the one clinical TFL layout, not a
general-purpose RTF library.  What that buys you:

- **One output style, opinionated defaults.**  No theme zoo, no
  "render anything" pipeline.  The defaults match the conventional
  clinical TFL look out of the box; you do not have to assemble it.
- **Only the features TFL → RTF needs.**  Multi-section headers /
  footers, spanning column headers, automatic page-number fields
  (`{PAGE}` / `{TOTAL_PAGES}`), embedded figures, and
  per-document concatenation via `assemble_rtf()`.  If a feature
  would not appear on a real clinical TFL, we resist adding it.
- **Maintainability over breadth.**  Saying *no* to scope creep is
  what keeps the package small, the tests fast, and the API stable.
- **Composable pipe API.**  `rtf_document() |> rtf_section() |>
  rtf_tables() |> generate_rtfreport()` — the same vocabulary every
  time, so building a 50-TFL deliverable is a loop.

If your deliverables need a substantially different layout, another tool
may serve you better — and that trade-off is intentional.  We would
rather do one well-defined style really well than do everything passably.
You are warmly welcome to use rtfreporter for the styles it supports.

## Why RTF?

RTF is an old format, and we are perfectly aware of that.  Producing
`.docx` directly, or rendering straight to PDF, is entirely possible and
in some respects more modern.  We chose RTF on purpose, for the most
old-fashioned of reasons: **it is the simplest thing that fully meets the
need.**

For clinical deliverables the workflow we care about is
**RTF → (optional post-processing) → PDF**, and that route is still
genuinely useful today:

- **Simple grammar.**  RTF is plain text with a small, well-understood
  command vocabulary.  That keeps the renderer small and auditable —
  which matters in a regulated setting.
- **Easy to patch when you must.**  Because the output is just text, a
  last-minute correction can be made by hand or by a small script,
  without round-tripping through a binary editor.
- **Universally openable.**  Every word processor opens RTF and exports
  it to PDF, so the final step fits whatever your organisation already
  uses.

A PDF-first or DOCX-first toolkit could do the same job, perhaps more
elegantly or with more features.  But for *our* needs — which are modest,
specific, and well-defined — RTF remains the easiest path that is
**necessary and sufficient**.  Simplicity, here, is the feature.

## Status

Pre-1.0 (`lifecycle: experimental`): the latest release is `v0.8.2`, and

the site's sidebar.

## Citation

If rtfreporter helps your work, please cite it:

```r
citation("rtfreporter")
```

If the numbers in your tables come from a [cards](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/) /
[cardx](https://insightsengineering.github.io/cardx/) ARD, please cite those
packages too (`citation("cards")`, `citation("cardx")`): they compute the
statistics; rtfreporter only lays them out.
